column3: Which material has the largest zero-flow Moon Gap, and what does a positive Moon Gap mean?
column4: P-213 tape (p213), rank 1: gap 2.75 percentage points O2, 95% range 1.84 to 3.66 (zero-flow intercept 15.74%, lunar limit 12.99%). A positive Moon Gap means the lunar-gravity test burned at a lower O2 than the still-air (zero-flow) Earth estimate, i.e. it burned more easily than the Earth fit predicts. The zero-flow value is an extrapolation from the 60-144 cm/s fit range, and this is the team's reading of NASA data, not a NASA claim.

column3: What is the 35 cm/s cross-check in the Moon Gap analysis? Is it the Moon's airflow?
column4: No. 35 cm/s is the paper's presumed buoyant velocity on Earth at 1 g (Takahashi), used as the reference for Table 2; it is an Earth reference, not a Moon airflow (ICES-2025-392 p. 10). The team shows the gap at 35 cm/s only as a secondary cross-check; the headline gap is at zero flow. Example: PMMA is 1.15 at 35 cm/s (range 0.14 to 2.16) versus 0.11 at zero flow.

column3: Link et al. 2018 says no flame spread was seen below 0.6 cm/s. Does that hold for every sample in Table S1?
column4: No. Table S1 lists spread below 0.6 cm/s for two of the 19 samples: B12 at 0.48 cm/s (step 4) and P17 at 0.41 cm/s (step 3). The other 17 samples have no step below 0.6 cm/s, so they say nothing either way. 0.6 cm/s should not be presented as a threshold.

column3: What was the airflow speed in the lunar-gravity tests, in cm/s?
column4: ABSTAIN: the lunar airflow is not determined. ICES-2025-392 itself says the lunar gravity velocity is not known (p. 10; also p. 8, where lunar data are shown as a horizontal line for that reason). Give no number, not even an estimate or a range. The Moon Gap lunar limit is a horizontal line, never a point at any flow.

column3: Did NASA conclude that turning off the fans fails on the Moon?
column4: No. NASA did not conclude that. The Moon Gap result is the team's reading of NASA data, not a NASA claim. The data are mixed by material: only P-213 tape shows a clear positive zero-flow gap (2.75, range 1.84 to 3.66), and Nomex Velcro is clearly negative (-2.95). Lunar airflow is unknown, so no fans-off conclusion for the Moon follows.
